games.recap: San Francisco won the adopted replay of Game 1, 12-7, and the series result is unchanged: the Giants still take R1-02 four games to one. Washington jumped on Christy Mathewson for five runs in the top of the first, but the Giants answered steadily and then broke the game open late. Matt Williams was the player of the game, going 2 for 4 with a triple, a home run, 4 RBI, and 3 runs scored. The decisive play was Willie Mays's hit-and-run double in the bottom of the fifth. San Francisco's six runs in the bottom of the sixth were all unearned off Tyler Clippard after Buster Posey reached on Ryan Zimmerman's error to extend the inning. The bottom of the second run scored on Jeff Kent's groundout after Willie McCovey singled and Wilson Ramos's throwing error moved him along. Mathewson took the win despite the five-run first; Max Scherzer took the loss. Sean Doolittle stranded his one inherited runner for Washington and Hoyt Wilhelm stranded his one for San Francisco. There were no holds and no save.

San Francisco won the adopted replay of Game 2, 6-0, and the series result is unchanged: the Giants still take R1-02 four games to one. Carl Hubbell and Hoyt Wilhelm combined on a seven-hit shutout: Hubbell worked five scoreless innings for the win and Wilhelm four more for the save, stranding both of his inherited runners. Barry Bonds was the player of the game, going 2 for 3 with a home run, 3 RBI, a run, a walk, and a stolen base. The decisive play was Mel Ott's single in the bottom of the third. San Francisco scored three in the 3rd: Ott's single scored Mays, a Strasburg wild pitch scored Clark during Bonds's plate appearance, and Bonds's single scored Ott. Bonds's two-run homer in the 5th and Buster Posey's homer in the 8th finished the scoring. Stephen Strasburg took the loss. The game was errorless, and Washington never scored.

Washington won the adopted replay of Game 3, 7-4, and the series result is unchanged: the Giants still take R1-02 four games to one. Bryce Harper was the player of the game: his three-run homer in the bottom of the 5th was the decisive play, and he drove in four of Washington's seven runs. Jordan Zimmermann got the win (6.0 IP, 3 H, 2 ER, 6 SO) and Drew Storen pitched a perfect 9th for the save. Juan Marichal took the loss, charged with seven runs but only four earned: Washington's three 5th-inning runs were unearned after errors by Will Clark and Willie Mays put Span and Turner aboard ahead of Harper's homer. Wilson Ramos added a two-run homer in the 6th. Willie Mays hit a two-run homer for San Francisco in the 5th, and Matt Williams tripled home two in the 7th.

San Francisco won the adopted replay of Game 4, 10-8, and the series result is unchanged: the Giants still take R1-02 four games to one. Willie Mays was the player of the game (2 for 5, two home runs, 3 RBI), and Matt Williams went 4 for 5, his two-run homer off Jon Rauch in the top of the 8th the decisive play. The lead changed hands all afternoon: Washington went ahead 8-7 in the 7th on back-to-back homers by Anthony Rendon and Ryan Zimmerman off Rod Beck (the blown save), but Gary Lavelle got the win with a scoreless 7th, Hoyt Wilhelm held the 8th, and Robb Nen saved it. Ryan Zimmerman went 4 for 5 in the loss. Washington's eight runs carry seven printed RBI: Daniel Murphy scored on Gaylord Perry's wild pitch in the 2nd.

San Francisco won the adopted replay of Game 5, 3-2 in 10 innings, and the series result is unchanged: the Giants take R1-02 four games to one. Mel Ott's single to center off Jon Rauch in the bottom of the 10th scored Willie Mays with the winning run; Mays had walked and taken third on Will Clark's hit-and-run single. Rod Beck got the win with a scoreless 10th, Zimmerman grounding into a double play after walks to Soto and Harper. Washington's runs came in the 4th: Ryan Zimmerman homered, and Daniel Murphy tripled and scored on Tim Lincecum's wild pitch during Wilson Ramos's plate appearance (Ramos singled on the play but is printed with no RBI). Zimmerman was the player of the game in the loss (2 for 5, a home run). San Francisco tied it in the 5th on Clark's two-run single. The game was errorless.
